summary: Bayer AG authors describe Ascent, a deployed MCP server with 31 tools: database and schema discovery, medical coding, question answering with an answerability check and 'Clues' disambiguation, cohort building, and literature. It is used from LibreChat, Claude Code and Cursor over de-identified Optum EHR data in Snowflake under per-user grants. EpiTrap is the authors' own set of 156 native / 153 OMOP questions; each targets one known epidemiological error and is graded by two LLM judges. On it, agent loops with Sonnet 5 or DeepSeek-V4-Pro beat a fixed one-pass pipeline by ~27 pp (native) and ~20 pp (OMOP) at more tool calls, while gpt-oss-120b did not. Reflection prompts helped only in one framework, and removing the specialized text-to-SQL tools left Sonnet 5 accuracy unchanged.

claims.claim: With capable models, agents beat the fixed pipeline by an average of 27 and 20 percentage points
claims.evidence: Table 2 with paired question-level bootstrap: +26.7 pp native [18.7,35.0], +20.4 pp OMOP [13.3,27.5], averaged over ten Sonnet 5/DeepSeek configurations; gpt-oss stays near baseline. The pipeline has no revision step and is not compute-matched (acknowledged). Apparently one run per configuration. Grading is by LLM judges only, on author-built, LLM-drafted rubrics.

claims.claim: Reflection prompting adds cost without consistent accuracy gains
claims.evidence: Table 2: reflection helps Claude Agent SDK (75->83 native, 75->82 OMOP) but not LangGraph or Strands; +27% tool calls and +13% runtime on average. Single runs make few-point differences uninterpretable.

claims.claim: Specialized text-to-SQL tooling reduces tool calls but does not improve accuracy for a frontier model
claims.evidence: Table 2 'no scaffold' (Sonnet 5, Claude Agent SDK only): 76/84 vs 75/75 plain and 81/84 vs 83/82 reflect, with 1.5-2.1x more calls. One model, one framework, single run. Discovery, coding and SQL execution tools stay available in both arms.

claims.claim: Real use shows value for feasibility assessment, diagnostic iteration and expert-guided analysis; tasks that took days or weeks were done within sessions
claims.evidence: §6: 36 users and 13,002 calls (12 July-21 Sept 2026), logged sessions and researcher-authored use-case reports. No outcome measures or comparison; the time savings are self-reported.

claims.claim: The shared MCP tool surface makes the system portable and model-agnostic
claims.evidence: The same production server was driven by three orchestrators x three models in evaluation and by LibreChat, Cursor and Claude Code in use. Portability is demonstrated; no benefit over a non-MCP integration is measured.

patterns.note: One governed MCP server is consumed unchanged by three orchestration frameworks, three models and three client hosts. Portability is shown by use; there is no comparison with alternatives.

Discovery tools (list databases, machine-readable schema, sample rows, row counts) and staged feasibility checks before committing to an analysis. Supported only by qualitative field reports; 'a defensible negative finding' is called valuable but not measured.

Agent receives M-Schema with sampled values and value distributions, a map of ontology-coded columns, a clinical vocabulary index, and provenance-tracked reusable code lists. The 'no scaffold' ablation keeps these, so their contribution is not isolated.

'Clues' surfaces consequential interpretations (population, denominator, time window) for the user to confirm before SQL is written. Not ablated, and the paper does not say how it behaved in unattended EpiTrap runs.
Optional on-demand skills for vetted workflows and database quirks (coding formats, date semantics). Not stated whether they were loaded during EpiTrap; not ablated.

A fixed one-pass pipeline loses by 20-27 pp to agent loops with capable models and ties with gpt-oss. The pipeline has no retry or validation stage and is not compute-matched, so it is a weak static baseline.
Single-agent tool loops beat the fixed pipeline only with capable models, and only against a weak, non-compute-matched baseline.

SQL self-heals on execution errors. The field lesson is that consequential errors passed execution and returned plausible numbers, so execution success was not an adequate correctness gate (qualitative).
Evaluation uses two LLM judges (kappa .62 native, .75 OMOP) with an Opus adjudicator, and no human validation. Anthropic models both generate OMOP SQL and judge.
36 users and 13,002 calls over ~10 weeks; qualitative workflow and failure-mode reports, no outcome metrics.

methodology.sample: EpiTrap: 156 native Optum-EHR and 153 OMOP questions, one designed-in error each, LLM-drafted and author-edited. Field: 36 users, 13,002 calls.
methodology.baselines: Fixed mechanical pipeline (generate SQL, resolve codes, execute, verbalize; no revision); not compute-matched
methodology.models: Orchestrators: Sonnet 5, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, gpt-oss-120b under Claude Agent SDK (Sonnet only), LangGraph, Strands. Services: Opus 4.8 (OMOP SQL), Gemini 3.6 Flash (native SQL). Judges: Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Luna; adjudicator: Opus 4.8.
methodology.variance: Paired question-level bootstrap CIs for averaged gains only; no repeated runs reported per configuration
methodology.ablations: Plain vs reflect prompt; withholding specialized text-to-SQL tools (Sonnet 5 / Claude Agent SDK only). Clues, skills and the medical coder are not ablated.
methodology.contamination_controls: New author-built questions; no control for judge self-preference (Anthropic models both build SQL and grade)
methodology.languages: SQL on Snowflake (OMOP-CDM and native Optum schema); natural-language questions

standards.artifacts: Ascent demo code and EpiTrap questions/rubrics released at github.com/bayer-group/ascent-epi-demo; patient data proprietary (Optum)

biases.detail: The authors' system is evaluated on the authors' dataset, with rubrics drafted by LLMs and edited by the authors.
No human grading. Inter-judge kappa is .62 on native. Opus-family models generate part of the SQL and adjudicate.
The fixed pipeline cannot revise or validate and is not compute-matched (acknowledged).
One run per configuration; few-point framework and reflection differences cannot be separated from noise.
Field claims ('days or weeks' compressed into sessions) come from researcher-authored use-case reports.
Time and tool calls are reported, but tokens and dollar cost are not.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Ascent (authors' in-house system); third-party models from Anthropic, DeepSeek, OpenAI, Google
coi.detail: A pharma company, not an AI vendor, promotes its own deployed system on its own benchmark with LLM grading and no independent replication. The headline comparison is between its own configurations.

verdict_reason: A real deployment, multiple models and frameworks, bootstrap CIs, a useful 'no scaffold' ablation, and released code and questions. Against that: a self-built LLM-graded benchmark, single runs, a weak non-compute-matched baseline, and no ablation of the discovery, clarification and domain-context components that matter most for this scope.
applicability: This is the batch's closest analogue for a healthcare-content team on mixed hosts. One governed MCP server exposes discovery (list sources, machine-readable schemas, sample rows, value distributions), domain vocabulary lookup, and persisted, provenance-tracked artifacts reused across analyses (a form of knowledge capture). Claude Code, Cursor and a chat UI all use it unchanged. The team's equivalent would be a content-domain MCP server over ingestion schemas, the educational-content taxonomy, and the contracts between the 4+ repos, plus skills for repo and database quirks. Three cautions. First, Clues-style clarification and the skills were never ablated, so this does not show that asking before acting helps. Second, with a frontier model the bespoke text-to-SQL generators added no accuracy, which favours investing in discovery and domain-knowledge tools over bespoke generators. Third, execution success was not a correctness gate (plausible answers to the wrong question), so acceptance checks must encode domain semantics, not just tests passing.
